newsitem.title: FINLAND: Profit-takers sink Helsinki but recovery expected.
newsitem.headline: Profit-takers sink Helsinki but recovery expected.

text.p: Shares slipped broadly on Wednesday amid calm profit-taking but top insurers rose after reporting unsurprising but good 1996 results, brokers said.

After rising 20 percent this year to break the psychologically important 3,000 point barrier on Tuesday, the HEX general index closed at 2,976.10 points, down one percent. Volume was a moderate 625 million markka.
The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark was down 1.16 percent at 1,039.35 points.
"There was no specific reason for today's losses, players just decided it was a good time to pocket some profits," said one broker.
"This is a short-term fluctuation. The market could easily turn in the opposition direction tomorrow or the day after," said another broker.

Bourse engine Nokia eased 3.50 markka to 323.50, but forestries were particularly hard hit by profit-taking with UPM-Kymmene -- which has led the recent rally -- down 4.00 markka at 111.00. The forestry sub-index fell 3.27 percent.

Both leading insurers Pohjola and Sampo reported higher 1996 profits and expected growth in premiums in 1997, but Sampo outperformed its rival on a sligthly more positive outlook and a planned four-for-one share split.
"Sampo has a bit stronger growth, and it is more optimistic in its outlook," one broker said.
"The insurance companies have done well. They both came out with good results, and even Merita rose in their wake before falling back," one broker said.
Merita closed up 0.10 at 19.00 after hitting 19.50 intra-session -- the highest ever for Merita, formed through the merger of Unitas and KOP in 1995.
